शुतुद्रि शुतु-द्रि, इस्, f. (according to Sāy.
fr. शु = क्षिप्रम् + तु = तुन्ना with rt. द्रु), the
Śatadru or Sutlej river. See शत-द्रु.
शुतु-द्री, f., Ved. = शुतु-द्रि.
शुतु-द्रु, उस्, or शुतु-द्रू, ऊस्, f. = शुतु-द्रि.

शूतिपर्ण शूति-पर्ण, अस्, m. (the meaning
of शूति is doubtful), a kind of tree (= आरग्-बध).
शूति, इस्, f. swelling, increasing.

सुति, इस्, f. extracting or pouring out the Soma
juice, &c.

1. सूति, इस्, f. (for 2. see p. 1118, col. 1), a place
where Soma juice is poured out or extracted (=
सोमाभिषव-भूमि, according to Śabda-k.).

2. सूति, इस्, f. (for 1. see p. 1117, col. 3; for 3. see
p. 1131), birth, production, delivery, child-bearing,
parturition, bringing forth; offspring, progeny.
—सूति-
गृह, अम्, n. the lying-in chamber, (also written
सूती-गृह.)
—सूति-मास or सूती-मास, अस्, m. the
month of delivery, the last month of gestation or
pregnancy (= वैजनन).
—सूत्य्-आशौच, अम्, n.
impurity caused by child-birth (continuing for ten
days in the case of regular parturition, and in the
case of a miscarriage for a period of days equal to
the number of months elapsed since conception).

सुती, ईस्, m. f. (abl. gen. sing. सुत्युस्), one who
wishes for a son; one who treats like a son.
सुती सुती. See p. 1118, col. 1.
सूती. See under 2. सूत above.

सूत-तनय, अस्, m. the son of a charioteer; epi-

1. सुत्या, f. Soma pressing, Soma preparation [cf.

2. सुत्या, f. bringing forth a child, parturition.
सुत्या. See p. 1118, col. 1.
सूत्या सूत्या. See under rt. 3. सु, p. 1117.

सुत्वन्, आ, m. an offerer of Soma juice; a drinker

सुत्वन् सुत्वन्. See under rt. 3. सु, p. 1117.

सुतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having or possessing a child, hav-

—सूतका-गृह, अम्,
n. a part of a house appropriated to a woman in

—सूतिका-षष्ठी,

f. a particular goddess worshipped on the sixth day

सूत्पर सूत्पर, अम्, n. the distilling of

सूत्र् सूत्र् (probably to be regarded as a
Nom. fr. सूत्र below; see सूत्रय,
col. 3), cl. 10. P. सूत्रयति, सूत्रापयति, &c., to
tie, bind, thread, string; to unbind, relax: Intens.
सोसूत्र्यते.

सूत्र, अम्, n. (fr. rt. सिव्, ‘to sew;’ but said to
be connected with rt. सूत्र् above), a thread, string,
line, cord; fibre, wire; a collection of threads; the
sacred thread or cord worn by the first three classes,
(see यज्ञोपवीत, p. 804); the string or wire of a
puppet or doll; a short rule or precept, axiom,
aphorism (in morals, religion, or science; इति सू-
त्रेण, according to such an aphorism); a short and
technical sentence or metrical line used as a memorial
rule to aid in the acquirement of any system (and
hence generally expressed in brief and obscure and
sometimes symbolical language, intelligible only to
those who possess the key to its interpretation, this
key being sometimes given in separate Sūtras called
Paribhāṣās, and the right understanding of a whole
series or chain of rules depending on a knowledge of
the Adhikāra or heading-rule and its influence [अनु-
वृत्ति] on those that follow; these short sentences
and aphoristic rules, the use of which constitutes a
most curious feature in the literary history of the
Hindūs, appear to have been often mere aids to the
memory of teachers — mere hints to guide lecturers in
their oral explications; they were also especially
useful in this way to the priests who had the
management of a complicated ritual); any work or
manual consisting of strings or long lines of the
above aphoristic rules and sentences hanging toge-
ther like threads, (though the term सूत्र may
possibly indicate not so much a line or series of
rules as rules written on leaves which were kept
together by strings; these Sūtra works form a sort
of groundwork or foundation of teaching, not only
in all religious ritual, but in philosophy, in grammar,
and in the collateral subjects of accent, euphony,
etymology, and prosody: thus in religion and ritual
there are first the Śrauta-sūtras, and among them
principally the Kalpa-sūtras, founded directly on
Śruti, q. v., and treating especially of ritual; they
form a kind of rubric or directory to Vedic cere-
monial, or in other words, a complete systema-
tized guide to the rambling discursive Brāhmaṇa as
distinct from the Mantra portion of the Veda [see
ब्राह्मण], giving concise rules for the perform-
ance of every kind of sacrifice; there are Sūtras of
this kind by Āśvalāyana and Śāṅkhāyana for the
Ṛg-veda; by Kātyāyana for the White Yajur-veda;
by Āpastamba, Baudhāyana, and the Mānavas for
the Black Yajur-veda; by Lāṭyāyana, Drāhyāyaṇa,
Maśaka, and Gobhila for the Sāma-veda; and by
Kuśika for the Atharva-veda; there are also two
other kinds of Sūtras connected with ceremonial,
viz. the Grihya-sūtras and Sāmayācārika or Dharma-
sūtras [often by the same authors, with special refer-
ence also to each separate Veda, and even placed by
some, like the Kalpa, under the head of Sūtras
founded on Śruti], which are really ‘rules for domestic
ceremonies and conventional customs,’ and are some-
times called collectively Smārta-sūtras [as founded
on स्मृति or ‘tradition,’ see स्मार्त]; these led to
the later Dharma-śāstras or ‘law-books’ attributed
to Manu, Yājñavalkya, Parāśara, &c., the names of
the authors of the Sūtras and of the law-books being
often identical; in philosophy each system has its
regular text-book of aphorisms written in Sūtras by
its supposed founder, see वेदान्त-सूत्र, न्याय-स्˚,
[]
साङ्ख्य-स्˚, मीमांसा-स्˚, वैशेषिक-स्˚, योग-स्˚;
in Vyākaraṇa or grammar there are the celebrated
Sūtras of Pāṇini in eight books, which are the
groundwork of a vast grammatical literature, besides
the Uṇādi-sūtras on certain affixes; in Vedic accent
and phonetics there are the Prātiśākhyas [see प्राति-
शाख्य] and the Phiṭ-sūtras of Śāntanava; in
etymology there are strings of Vedic words, and
in prosody there are the Sūtras of Piṅgala-nāga on
Chandas, including both Vedic and non-Vedic
metres, and the Nidāna-sūtra on the metres of the
Sāma-veda and Vedic metres generally: it should be
borne in mind that the mixture of Ślokas in some
of the Prātiśākhyas and in some more recent Sūtra
works, though depriving them of the brevity strictly
necessary to constitute Sūtras, does not prevent their
being regarded as collections of aphoristic and me-
morial rules: with regard to grammatical Sūtras it is
necessary to remember that all connecting words
used as prepositions, however necessary to the sense,
are omitted; thus, a word in the genitive case re-
quires स्थाने, ‘instead of,’ to be supplied; a word in
the ablative requires परम्, ‘after;’ a word in the
instrumental requires सह, ‘together with;’ a word
in the locative, though sometimes to be translated
in the ordinary way by prefixing ‘in,’ may often be
used as a locative absolute, and परे must then be
supplied, the sense being ‘on such an affix or word
coming after or following;’ the word वा is equivalent
to ‘optionally’ or ‘alternative’); any rule, law, canon,
decree (in law &c.).
—सूत्र-कण्ठ, अस्, m. ‘hav-
ing Sūtras in the throat or mouth ready to be
repeated,’ a Brāhman; ‘having lines on the throat,’
a pigeon, dove; a wagtail.
—सूत्र-कर्मन्, अ, n.
‘rule-work,’ carpentry.
—सूत्र-कार, अस्, m. the
author or composer of Sūtras.
—सूत्र-कृत्, त्, m.
‘Sūtra-maker,’ the author of an aphorism or set of
aphorisms.
—सूत्र-कोण or सूत्र-कोणक, अस्, m.
a small drum shaped like an hour-glass and struck
by a string and button (= डमरु).
—सूत्र-
गण्डिका, f. a kind of stick used by weavers in

—सूत्र-ग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, hold-
ing a thread.
—सूत्र-ग्राह, अस्, ई, अम्, taking a
thread.
—सूत्र-चरण, N. of a class of Caraṇas or
Vedic schools who introduced various Sūtra works.
—सूत्र-तन्तु, उस्, m. a thread, string, line.
—सू-
त्र-तर्कुटी, f. a distaff, spindle.
—सूत्र-धर,
अस्, m. = सूत्र-धार.
—सूत्र-धार, अस्, m. ‘rule-
holder, thread-holder,’ a stage-manager, a director or
principal actor who arranges the plot of a drama
and takes a leading part in the prelude; a carpenter;
the author of a set of rules or aphorisms; epithet of
Indra.
—सूत्र-पिटक, अस्, m., N. of one of the
three collections of Buddhist writings (viz. those
which prescribe rules for the laity, see त्रि-पिटक).
—सूत्र-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘thread-flowered,’ the
cotton plant.
—सूत्र-भिद्, त्, m. ‘thread-cutter,’ a
tailor.
—सूत्र-भृत्, त्, m. = सूत्र-धार.
—सू-
त्र-मध्य-भू, ऊस्, f. ‘born amid threads or
fibres,’ the resin or Shorea Robusta; incense.
—सू-
त्र-यन्त्र, अम्, n. ‘thread-machine,’ a shuttle; a
weaver's loom.
—सूत्र-विद्, त्, m. ‘a Sūtra-knower,’
one versed in Sūtras.
—सूत्र-वीणा, f. a kind of lute
(= लाबुकी).
—सूत्र-वेष्टन, अम्, n. a weaver's
shuttle; the act of weaving.
—सूत्रात्मन् (˚र-आत्˚),
आ, आ, अ, having the nature of a string or thread;
(आ), m. ‘soul-thread,’ intellect having for its site the
collective totality of subtile bodies; the soul.
—सू-
त्राली (˚र-आली), f. a string of beads &c. worn round
the neck, necklace.

सूत्रण, अम्, n. the act of stringing together, ar-
ranging, putting in order; arranging in aphorisms.

सूत्रय, Nom. P. सूत्रयति, सूत्रयाम्-आस,
सूत्रयितुम्, to make a Sūtra or aphorism, arrange
in the form of an aphorism, prescribe or declare in

सूत्रला, f. a spindle, distaff.
सूत्रिका, f. a kind of dish or cake.

सूत्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, having threads or lines, having
rules; (ई), m. a crow.
सूत्रामन् सूत्रामन्, आ, m. = सु-त्रामन्.
